Positive real numbers \( x, y, \) and \( z \) satisfy the following equations:

\[
xyz = 3,
\]
\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x) = 4,
\]
\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x) = 40.
\]

Compute the minimum possible value for \( x \).

Give the minimum value of x as an exact expression using only integers, rational numbers, and radicals (no trigonometric or inverse trigonometric functions, and no approximations).

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(a<b<c\) be the increasing rearrangement of any solution \((x,y,z)\).

The expression \((x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\) is alternating, so its square is unchanged by permutation. Since its given value is \(4\), its square is \(16\). For the increasing order,
\[
(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)>0,
\]
so
\[
(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)=4.
\]
The other two equations are symmetric, so \((a,b,c)\) is also a solution. Therefore the minimum possible value of \(x\) is the minimum possible smallest entry of a solution. Hence we may assume
\[
x<y<z.
\]

Set
\[
r=\frac yx>1,\qquad s=\frac zy>1,\qquad P=rs=\frac zx>1.
\]
Then
\[
y=rx,\qquad z=rsx=Px,
\]
and from \(xyz=3\),
\[
x^3=\frac{3}{rP}.
\]

Now
\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)
=x^3r(1-r)(1-s)(P-1)
=\frac{3}{P}(1-r)(1-s)(P-1),
\]
so
\[
(P-1)(1-r)(1-s)=\frac{4P}{3}.
\]
Also
\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x)
=x^3r(1+r)(1+s)(P+1)
=\frac{3}{P}(1+r)(1+s)(P+1),
\]
so
\[
(P+1)(1+r)(1+s)=\frac{40P}{3}.
\]

Let \(S=r+s\). Since
\[
(1-r)(1-s)=P+1-S,
\qquad
(1+r)(1+s)=P+1+S,
\]
we get
\[
(P-1)(P+1-S)=\frac{4P}{3},
\]
\[
(P+1)(P+1+S)=\frac{40P}{3}.
\]
Eliminating \(S\),
\[
\frac{40P}{3(P+1)}-(P+1)
=P+1-\frac{4P}{3(P-1)}.
\]
This simplifies to
\[
3P^3-19P^2+15P-3=0,
\]
and hence
\[
(3P-1)(P^2-6P+3)=0.
\]
Because \(P>1\), we must have
\[
P=3+\sqrt6.
\]
Then
\[
S=4+\frac{\sqrt6}{3}.
\]
Thus \(r,s\) are the roots of
\[
t^2-St+P=0.
\]
Its discriminant is
\[
S^2-4P
=\left(2-\frac{\sqrt6}{3}\right)^2,
\]
so
\[
\{r,s\}=\left\{3,\;1+\frac{\sqrt6}{3}\right\}.
\]

Since
\[
x^3=\frac{3}{rP},
\]
for fixed \(P\) the value of \(x\) is minimized by taking the larger value of \(r\), namely \(r=3\). Therefore
\[
x^3=\frac{3}{3(3+\sqrt6)}
=\frac1{3+\sqrt6}
=\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}.
\]
Thus the minimum possible value of \(x\) is
\[
\boxed{\sqrt[3]{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}}}.
\]
